Subject: Planning window for upcoming private deployment patches

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the support on our private deployment. We want to schedule the Q1 maintenance to apply two security patches (model runtime and OS kernels) and also pin service images to the current compatible runtime. Can you share the typical maintenance window you recommend for VPC/on-prem customers and what rollback guarantees Redwood provides?

Specific asks:
- Recommended maintenance window (duration + preferred days/times for east-coast operations)
- Expected downtime or degraded latency behavior during the patch (per-service SLO impacts)
- Steps to trigger a rollback and estimated RTO (minutes)
- Any change-order or procurement paperwork we should sign ahead of time

We can be flexible this quarter but need the runbook and rollback steps by end of next week.

Thanks,
Caroline Nguyen
Senior Platform Ops, Finlytics

From: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-16T13:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Planning window for upcoming private deployment patches

Hi Caroline — thanks for the clear list. Draft responses below and attached a first-pass runbook (private-maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf).

High-level recommendation:
- Window: 02:00–06:00 ET (overnight maintenance improves rollback options and reduces user traffic). For Finlytics traffic patterns, we recommend Saturday 02:00–06:00 ET for a full patch; weekday late-night can be used for canaries.
- Expected user impact: we aim for degraded latency rather than hard downtime for stateless endpoints. For stateful workflows (indexing/long-running inference jobs) we recommend draining and pausing ingest for the 30 minutes prior to patch start.
- Rollback: Two-tier fallback — (1) automated image rollback to pinned pre-patch tag; (2) manual cluster snapshot restore (only if image rollback fails). Typical automated image rollback RTO: ~8–18 minutes depending on KV cache and session rehydration. Manual restore RTO: 45–90 minutes.

Plan items attached: runbook, run-of-show, and a checklist for firewall/NAT rules to validate connectivity after kernel updates. We will pin the runtime image to the last-known-good digest during the maintenance window; we recommend Finlytics confirm if you want us to keep a longer pin (30 days) or a short pin (7 days) after the patch for validation.

Next steps / asks for Finlytics:
- Confirm maintenance weekend preference (Sat vs Sun)
- Provide a primary on-call for the weekend (name + mobile)
- Sign change-order draft if you want Redwood to perform the patch under a covered change (we've attached a draft: change-order-draft.docx).

Attaching: private-maintenance-runbook-v2.pdf

Thanks — happy to iterate on the runbook.

Regards,
Dylan Brooks
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Looping in network and runtime. Quick notes on networking and compliance checks (I'll attach a trimmed runbook snippet).

Laura's notes:
- Firewall/NAT: Confirm customer NAT timeouts for long-lived SSH or admin sessions. If their NAT idles at 5 minutes, we should use agent-based health checks rather than SSH tunnels during the window.
- Segmentation: Ensure the private control-plane certificate remains valid for rollback; include a pre-check to validate cert expiry > 30 days.
- SOC evidence: Finlytics asked for rollback guarantees — include explicit audit log extracts in the runbook (timestamped image roll events + operator id).
- Canary approach: Do a 1-node canary in a non-prod AZ first for 45 minutes before the full roll. If latency increases > 20% or error rate > 0.8% on the canary, auto-abort and rollback.

Attachment: rollback-playbook.md (excerpt)

On the pin duration: recommend 7-day pin by default, extend to 30 only if the customer needs longer validation window. Also add an explicit step to flush KV cache after rollback to avoid stale embeddings returning inconsistent results.

Laura
Director, Site Reliability Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-01-17T09:20:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Planning window for upcoming private deployment patches

Adding operational commands and a short checklist for the rollback path (keeps everything reproducible). Copying the key steps here so Finlytics can see them in the runbook: 

Rollback (automated image revert) — summary commands:
- kubectl set image deployment/rdw-runtime rdw-runtime=rdw-runtime:<prepatch-digest> -n redwood
- wait-for: rollout status deployment/rdw-runtime --watch --timeout=900s
- post-checks: curl -sS https://<service>/health | jq '.uptime, .model_version'
- KV cache flush: POST https://admin.<customer-domain>/v1/cache/flush?namespace=kv --header 'X-Admin-Token: <token>'

If the automated rollback fails, manual restore steps (snapshot restore) are in rollback-playbook.md with estimated times. Recommend we include a step to capture the diagnostic bundle automatically on failure (kubectl bundle/gather + tar upload).

Operational caveat: If the kernel patch requires NIC firmware reload that impacts node reboots, the image rollback might succeed but node boot sequence could delay RTO — call this out explicitly in the runbook.

I'll add the above commands to the runbook and push an updated MD.

— Aditya
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
